Definition: adverb from G3956 and G3624; with the whole family:--with all his house.
BiblicalUsage: Panoiki means with the whole house, with all his family. The jailer brings Paul and Silas into his house, sets food before them, and rejoices, believing in God with all his house.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the whole house matters: the jailer's faith does not stop at his own heart, it fills his household, and they rejoice together.
RelatedEvents: Paul and Silas in the Philippian Prison
